title: Nginx Examples
description: Small Nginx examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Serving a static file
examples.description: Nginx is a web server. It can answer a request by sending a file, such as index.html, without running a custom application backend.
examples.code:
Request: GET /index.html
Nginx reads: the configured index.html file
Response: HTML for the browser

examples.title: Read the configuration structure
examples.description: Nginx configuration uses directives and blocks. Some directives are valid only in specific contexts.

examples.title: Document roots
examples.description: root chooses the base directory used to find a requested file. The request path is normally added to that base.

examples.title: Index documents
examples.description: index names files to try when a request refers to a directory. index.html is a common first page.

examples.title: Locations match request paths
examples.description: A location block chooses handling for matching request paths. Simple prefix locations are useful for organising a static site.

examples.title: Check files with try_files
examples.description: try_files checks candidate paths and uses a final fallback when none exists. Static generated pages often need directory index handling.

examples.title: Use a helpful error page
examples.description: A custom error page explains a missing route while retaining a useful HTTP status.

examples.title: Content types matter
examples.description: A MIME type tells the browser what kind of file it received. Standard Nginx MIME mappings cover common web assets.

examples.title: Cache deliberate file versions
examples.description: Caching lets browsers reuse files. Long caching works best for files whose names change when their contents change.

examples.title: Read access and error logs
examples.description: An access log records requests. An error log records problems such as missing permissions or invalid configuration.

examples.title: HTTPS protects the connection
examples.description: HTTPS uses TLS to encrypt traffic between the browser and server. A certificate identifies the hostname for that connection.
examples.code:
Browser -> encrypted HTTPS connection -> server
Certificate: must match the intended hostname
Keys: kept private on the server side

examples.title: Validate before reload
examples.description: A configuration test can catch syntax problems before the server tries to use a new configuration. Reloading is a separate action.
